items.title: `uv tool`: give users a flexible way to install tools with modifications
items.reason: Canonical maintainer-opened tracker for changing a tool’s additional requirements without retyping the complete `--with` list, using a declarative and fully resolved design.

items.title: Add `uv tool upgrade --with <new_pkg>` or `--add-with <new_pkg>` to add packages to an install
items.reason: Tracks the add/update half of the request: retaining existing additional packages while appending another one.

items.title: How to uninstall additional deps installed with a tool
items.reason: Covers removal and confirms that reinstalling with a new `--with` set removes omitted requirements, requiring users to repeat every requirement they want retained.

items.title: `uv tool install --in` to add packages to an existing tool environment
items.reason: Earlier proposal covering post-install add, upgrade, and uninstall operations. Maintainers rejected unsound in-place mutation, accepted a possible immutable declarative workflow, and closed it after opening astral-sh/uv#19980.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues plus open, closed, and merged pull requests using literal terms around `uv tool install`, `--with`, additional dependencies, add/remove/update, reinstall options, and tool environments; conceptual terms including plugins, injection/`pipx inject`, declarative tool configuration, receipts, upgrade, sync, and preserving prior requirements; and fix-oriented terms for `--show-with`, tool receipts, and environment modification. No matching implementation pull request was found. The canonical chain runs through astral-sh/uv#14746 and astral-sh/uv#7312 to astral-sh/uv#19980. astral-sh/uv#14143 was plausible but ruled out as canonical because it concerns retaining the original setup during reinstall, not editing the saved additional-requirement set; astral-sh/uv#7312 only established initial installation with `--with` and does not solve incremental changes.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#19980 already tracks the same underlying enhancement: a sound, declarative way to modify a tool installation’s extra requirements without reconstructing the entire prior `uv tool install ... --with ...` command. The new issue’s add/remove/update sketches and plugin examples fit within that tracker.
summary: astral-sh/uv#19980 is the canonical open tracker. astral-sh/uv#18996 and astral-sh/uv#15792 cover the narrower add and remove workflows, while closed astral-sh/uv#14746 records the design rationale and was superseded by the canonical tracker.
draft_response:
Thanks for the detailed use case. This is already tracked in astral-sh/uv#19980, which covers changing a tool’s additional requirements without having to reconstruct the complete prior `--with` invocation. The add-only workflow is also described in astral-sh/uv#18996, and the removal behavior is discussed in astral-sh/uv#15792.

The current design direction is to keep tool environments declarative and fully resolved rather than mutate them with an imperative injection operation, since in-place changes can leave the tool and plugin requirements inconsistent. The exact interface still needs design and a decision; astral-sh/uv#19980 is the place to continue that discussion. Closing this as a duplicate.
